subject: Urgent: production slowdown after canary swap (WhaleClient)
messages:
From: Alicia Stone <alicia.stone@whaleclient.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir.patel@whaleclient.com>
Date: Mon, 24 Jul 2028 09:32:00 -0700
Subject: Severe latency spike after today's canary

Hi Naomi,

We started seeing a significant slowdown in production shortly after Redwood flipped the canary to model v2.1 this morning. Key observations: p95 latency ~2x baseline, p99 ~3x baseline, error rate up from 0.3% to ~1.8%, and sustained throughput drop on our busiest routes. This is impacting user experience across our core search flows.

I've attached a CSV with percentile slices and timestamps. The timing lines up almost exactly with your canary rollout window. Can you confirm whether anything changed in the serving config (batching/kv cache/quantization) for v2.1? We need this escalated — our ops and product teams are watching.

Thanks,
Alicia
Alicia Stone
Head of Product
WhaleClient

Hi Alicia — thanks for the note and the attachment. I’m sorry you’re seeing this. I’m escalating to our on-call infra and engineering leads now (cc’d). We’ll open an incident bridge and run a quick check to see if the canary is correlated to config or kernel changes.

Proposed immediate next steps:
- Open a bridge and run live tracing across the impacted routes.
- If we confirm regression tied to v2.1, initiate canary rollback to v2.0 for WhaleClient only.
- Share a concise update within 30 minutes.

I’ll follow up once we have telemetry.

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 24 Jul 2028 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Severe latency spike after today's canary

Quick diagnostic notes after an initial look at telemetry:
- Observed a sharp rise in KV cache misses for WhaleClient routes coincident with the canary window. Miss rate jumps from ~6% to ~42%.
- Memory allocation patterns show higher peak GPU memory usage during generation for v2.1 (likely due to a change in attention kernel tiling).
- Continuous batching queuing time increased for short-sequence requests, pushing p95 up.

Immediate mitigation options:
A) Roll back WhaleClient to v2.0 for production (fastest).
B) If rollback not possible, route WhaleClient traffic to dedicated capacity or a compatibility variant with smaller memory footprint.

I’m attaching notes and the short query that pulled the metrics. I’ll stay on bridge for remediation.

Attachment: engineer_notes.txt (text)

—Marcus

What we’re doing now:
- Rolling WhaleClient back to v2.0 (rolling back 50% in the first 5 minutes, then 100% if metrics recover).
- Monitoring p95/p99/error rate and will post updates every 15 minutes on the bridge.
- After stabilizing, we’ll run a postmortem and share mitigation: kernel selector guardrails + additional canary checks.

We take this seriously — sorry for the disruption. I’ll post the first telemetry snapshot in 15 minutes.
